scenes.say: In 1932, Australia went to war against birds. And the birds won.
After World War One, veterans were given farmland in Western Australia to grow wheat.
Then around twenty thousand emus showed up, eating and trampling the crops.
So the government sent in soldiers, two machine guns, and ten thousand rounds of ammunition.
But the emus split into small groups, and ran at up to fifty kilometres an hour.
In one ambush, a gun jammed after only about a dozen birds.
By December, the army had fired nearly ten thousand rounds. That is about ten bullets per emu.
The soldiers went home. The emus stayed.
